objective: Validate minimum covered call execution feasibility.
finalConclusion: 0.01 BTC covered call is operationally feasible on Bybit Demo.

underlying.finding: Spot buy of 0.011 BTC produced net BTC >= 0.01 after BTC-denominated spot fee.

operationalFindings: Bybit Demo accepted a minimum BTC covered-call structure with BTC wallet coverage greater than 0.01 and short call quantity 0.01.
Spot BTC fee was charged in BTC, reducing net received BTC below requested gross quantity.
Buying exactly 0.01 BTC produced 0.00999 BTC net in an earlier test; 0.011 BTC provided sufficient net coverage.
The short call position was detected in the account with size 0.01 and avgPrice 10.
Open orders were zero after the acceptance test.
bugsFound: Spot fill classification initially depended too heavily on immediate execution-list/order-history availability.
The first option order attempt used an orderLinkId longer than Bybit's 36-character limit.
Baseline cleaning initially reduced excess assets but did not restore USDT to the target when USDT was below 2000.
bugsFixed: Separated order submission, fill detection, BTC balance delta, execution success, and coverage sufficiency.
Shortened option-sale orderLinkId prefix for future option order attempts.
Extended baseline clean to add missing USDT and reconcile back to the 2000 USDT target.
lessonsLearned: Minimum option quantity is 0.01 and can be represented by the selected weekly call.
Spot purchase sizing must account for BTC-denominated fees.
Execution probes need delayed/secondary evidence from wallet deltas and position detection, not only immediate fill lists.
Position detection is essential because option acceptance may be visible as an open short option position even when the local probe path sees later safety guards.
researchConclusions: Minimum covered call acceptance is operationally feasible in Bybit Demo.
This does not prove production viability, margin robustness, expiry behavior, settlement behavior, assignment mechanics, close workflow, or roll workflow.
Track B should now move from acceptance testing toward lifecycle research only after documenting close/settlement safeguards.
